text:
Armyworm (Spodoptera litura), rated as a high-importance pest.

Description: caterpillars are typically found on the underside of leaves, variably coloured with striping, and are mainly active at night, hiding during the day. Mature larvae reach roughly 3-4 cm in length. Eggs are laid in large masses (up to around 300 eggs per mass) covered with protective hair-like scales.

Damage: young larvae feed together in groups, initially skeletonising leaves; as they grow, larvae disperse and can cause severe defoliation, moving across a field in large numbers when populations are high (the origin of the "armyworm" name). Heavy infestations can also damage the growing point, causing significant yield loss.
